name: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Dāwūd al-Ṣanhājī, Ibn Ājurrūm
summary: Grammarian and teacher of Qurʾān recitation in Fez, author of al-Ājurrūmiyya, the most widely memorised first book of naḥw.
bio: Ibn Ājurrūm was born in Fez into a family of Ṣanhāja Berber origin; Ājurrūm is said to be a Berber word for a man of religion. He taught grammar and recitation in Fez, where he died in 723/1323.
His short Muqaddima, al-Ājurrūmiyya, sets out iʿrāb and the parts of the sentence in a few pages. More than sixty commentaries were written on it, and it reached Europe in the sixteenth century.
